reason: Choose A as the coherent composition direction: it keeps the crystal ball dominant while exposing the complete daily message at both sizes. Baseline retains stronger illustrated depth, navigation and supplied runtime evidence, hence its higher overall provisional scores. Preserve those strengths when considering A. B hides useful content and unavailable status; C gives the omen too much priority. No variant meets the requested threshold across every screen and component.
limitations: Component tuples use hierarchy, typography/spacing, surfaces/color, task clarity, feedback/recovery, accessibility. They cover both text sizes; material enlarged-text weaknesses are retained rather than averaged away.
Reviewed only supplied images, checks.json and expansion-31.html. No implementation, delegation, prior ratings or other graders were consulted.

Feedback scores for proposals assess visible content and state communication only. Orb runtime feedback and illustrative tab interaction are inapplicable to these composition prototypes and marked null. Static header feedback is also inapplicable. No reading, recovery action, focus lifecycle or disclosure interaction was independently driven.
Baseline runtime evidence is accepted as supplied and is not transferred to proposals. Different reading balances and orb appearance limit direct visual equivalence.

Checks establish consistent 261.3px proposal orbs and no horizontal overflow in twelve initial states. Source provides native disclosure semantics, focus styling and bottom padding, but does not prove scrolling, focus visibility or assistive-technology outcomes. Content below the initial viewport is not automatically unreachable.

Proposal navigation is illustrative and aria-hidden in source. Scores concern visible composition only: normal captures lack visible labels, and enlarged labels crowd the edges. These are not tested navigation controls.

No confirmed task-blocking hard gate is inferred from intentionally absent prototype functionality. Below-viewport content remains an untested reachability boundary, not a certified pass. Browser grades are provisional; physical iPhone, VoiceOver and native behavior remain unverified.
